ai.subject: Biochemistry & genetics
ai.summary: Thyroid peroxidase (TPO) iodinate tyrosines on thyroglobulin and couples iodinated residues to produce T3/T4. Autoantibodies to TPO cause Hashimoto’s thyroiditis, the most common cause of hypothyroidism.

sections.p: TPO is a membrane‑bound enzyme in the follicular cell apical membrane. It oxidizes iodide to iodine, iodinate thyroglobulin, and couples iodotyrosines to form T3 and T4.
Iodide enters via NIS, is oxidized by TPO, iodinated tyrosines on thyroglobulin form MIT/DIT, then coupled to produce T3/T4, stored in colloid.

t.b: Does not answer a TPO function; shows pituitary response to low thyroid hormone
Low indicates impaired hormone synthesis, often due to TPO dysfunction
Positive indicates autoimmune attack on TPO, leading to hypothyroidism

sections.p: TSH upregulates NIS, TPO, and thyroglobulin transcription. Iodine availability and intracellular calcium also modulate TPO activity.
Autoimmune destruction (Hashimoto’s) is the most common cause. Other causes include iodine deficiency, radiation, drugs (e.g., amiodarone), and genetic mutations.
Hypothyroidism presents with fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, and menstrual irregularities. Anti‑TPO antibodies predict progression to overt disease.

t.b: Elevated TSH with low free T4 confirms hypothyroidism
High titers predict autoimmune thyroiditis and risk of progression
Elevated LDL indicates metabolic impact of hypothyroidism

sections.p: Remember TPO is the target of anti‑TPO antibodies in Hashimoto’s. TPO catalyses both iodination and coupling steps. Low free T4 + high TSH = hypothyroidism.

whenToSeekHelp: Severe fatigue with weight gain and cold intolerance

faq.q: What causes anti‑TPO antibodies to develop?
faq.a: Autoimmune dysregulation, genetic predisposition, and environmental triggers such as iodine excess or infections.
Yes, rare mutations in the TPO gene cause congenital hypothyroidism.

faq.q: Why is TSH the first test?
faq.a: TSH is highly sensitive to changes in thyroid hormone levels and is inexpensive.

exam: Explain how TPO contributes to thyroid hormone synthesis.
